message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide that shows you **three** ways to spin up a new Compute Engine VM that has a high‑end NVIDIA GPU (the closest match to an “RTX A6000” that Google currently offers is the *Tesla A100*).  
(If you really need an RTX A6000 you’ll have to look at other providers – GCP does not list that exact SKU.)

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Pick a zone that supports GPUs (e.g. us-central1-a)
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create a project‑wide firewall rule that allows SSH (optional but handy)
gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-ssh \
    --allow tcp:22 \
    --direction INGRESS \
    --priority 1000 \
    --network default \
    --action ALLOW \
    --target-tags ssh-access

# 3. Spin up the instance
gcloud compute instances create gpu-demo \
    --zone $ZONE \
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM
    --subnet default \
    --tags ssh-access \
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 50GB \
    --boot-disk-type pd-balanced \
    --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
        apt-get update && apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
        echo "CUDA drivers installed." > /var/log/startup.log' \
    --accelerators type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
    --restart-on-failure
```

> **What this does**
> * Creates a VM named `gpu-demo` in `us-central1-a`.
> * Uses the `n1-standard-8` machine type (8 vCPU + 30 GiB RAM).
> * Attaches one *Tesla A100* GPU (`type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1`).
> * Installs CUDA drivers automatically via a startup script.
> * Sets the maintenance policy to terminate & restart on failure (good for spot‑like behavior).

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to hit the raw REST endpoint (or build your own wrapper), here’s the minimal JSON body:

```json
{
  "name": "gpu-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y cuda-drivers\n"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "automaticRestart": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE"
  }
}
```

Send it with a POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json
Body: <above JSON>
```

> Replace `YOUR_PROJECT`, `YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN`, and adjust the zone if needed.

---

## 3️⃣  Python Client Library (google-api-python-client)

```python
from googleapiclient import discovery
from oauth2client.client import GoogleCredentials

credentials = GoogleCredentials.get_application_default()
service = discovery.build('compute', 'v1', credentials=credentials)

project = 'YOUR_PROJECT'
zone = 'us-central1-a'

instance_body = {
    'name': 'gpu-demo',
    'machineType': f'zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8',
    'disks': [{
        'boot': True,
        'initializeParams': {
            'diskSizeGb': 50,
            'sourceImage': 'projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts'
        }
    }],
    'networkInterfaces': [{
        'network': 'global/networks/default',
        'accessConfigs': [{'type': 'ONE_TO_ONE_NAT', 'name': 'External NAT'}]
    }],
    'metadata': {
        'items': [{
            'key': 'startup-script',
            'value': '#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y cuda-drivers\n'
        }]
    },
    'serviceAccounts': [{
        'email': 'default',
        'scopes': ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform']
    }],
    'guestAccelerators': [{
        'acceleratorCount': 1,
        'acceleratorType': f'projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100'
    }],
    'scheduling': {
        'automaticRestart': False,
        'onHostMaintenance': 'TERMINATE'
    }
}

request = service.instances().insert(project=project, zone=zone, body=instance_body)
response = request.execute()
print(response)
```

> Make sure you’ve enabled the Compute Engine API and authenticated (e.g., `gcloud auth application-default login`).

---

### Quick Checklist

| Step | What to do |
|------|------------|
| 1 | Enable Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`) |
| 2 | Ensure billing is attached to your project |
| 3 | Verify the zone supports GPUs (`gcloud compute zones describe us-central1-a | grep supportedAcceleratorTypes`) |
| 4 | Run one of the snippets above |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it (`gcloud compute ssh gpu-demo --zone us-central1-a`) and verify the GPU:

```bash
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 470.57.02   Driver Version: 470.57.02   CUDA Version: 11.4     |
|-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
...
```

That’s all! Let me know if you’d like help setting up Docker, installing specific CUDA versions, or configuring persistent disks.
